clue.text: In a storm, ship may seek a diversion

definitions.meaning: a vessel in rough seas rocks fore and aft and is thrown about
an old gambling game of tossing coins at a mark, a pastime

explanation.walkthrough: The first stretch describes what a ship does in a storm; 'seek a' links it to the second sense, a coin-tossing game played for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a ship's rocking motion in heavy seas and a traditional coin-throwing pastime.

clue.text: With a kick, as in beer…

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other here

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer, standing for the drink
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as

explanation.surface: A beer with a bit of a kick to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next, which reuses the same trick with a different container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a kick is sharp and spicy to the taste, a synonym.

clue.text: … warm, as in a dram

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the drink word

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, like a dram

explanation.surface: A dram of whisky warms you up.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues 1 Down with the same pattern: a word for 'as' inside a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm something by a fire is to heat it through, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tom's Irish, relaxed and casual

indicators.note: relaxed suggests the letters loosened and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An easy-going Irishman called Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' looks like part of the description of Tom; it rearranges the letters of TOMS IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hit-or-miss is haphazard and unplanned, an idiom for careless or random.

clue.text: Badger in Noah's first vessel

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the name

parts.note: the ark was Noah's vessel

explanation.surface: An animal boarding Noah's Ark first.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger looks like the animal going aboard, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark someone is British slang for irritating or pestering them, as badger means to harass.

clue.text: Order disseminated — I dissent

indicators.note: disseminated means spread around, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an order being circulated.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows 'I dissent', a pronoun; its letter joins DISSENT to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness and good arrangement are what order means in a tidy room.

clue.text: By the sound of it, won over leather

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: someone won over has been swayed

explanation.surface: Someone is persuaded to buy leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is a soft napped kind of hide, a type of the material.

clue.text: Talk? Just the opposite!

definitions.meaning: the reverse or contrary of something

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation playfully suggests the answer means the opposite of talk; in fact it means both talk and opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hold a conversation; as a noun it means the reverse of a proposition.

clue.text: Fellow, following mistake, put in charge — there's irony for you

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A man is promoted after a blunder, which is ironic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irony' is read literally, as 'iron-y', made of or containing iron, not as wry humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric is the chemistry adjective for compounds containing iron, so literally iron-like.

clue.text: Cut up, being put into lodgings

definitions.meaning: divided into four pieces, as a carcass
billeted, as soldiers are housed in billets

explanation.definitionFit: It means both chopped into fourths and given accommodation, as troops in billets.

clue.text: Run away to marry east European on the rebound

indicators.note: on the rebound means bouncing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: Someone eloping with an east European after a failed affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' suggests a hasty marriage after a break-up; here it turns E plus POLE back to front, giving ELOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a direct description of eloping: secretly leaving to wed.

clue.text: Like a bird, following a ship

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird trailing behind a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means behind the vessel, at the rear, so trailing after it.

clue.text: Caught somebody out on inspection

indicators.note: out says the word is spread out to make room for a letter within it

parts.note: one means somebody, as in 'one does'
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
on and over both mean about, as in 'argue on/over a point'

explanation.surface: A batsman caught out during a match review.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a batsman is out caught; here 'Caught' is just C.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick once-over is a brief look or check, an idiom for a rapid examination.

clue.text: Jock's retreated in alarm

indicators.note: retreated means went backwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scot; the 's is 'has', giving no letter

explanation.surface: A Scotsman fleeing in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal, a synonym.

clue.text: Made quite an impression, processing such data

indicators.note: processing means working on something, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone impressed by crunching through a pile of data.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is an idiom for looking stylish and impressive.

clue.text: Strange coteries forming in secret

indicators.note: strange means odd or changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Odd cliques meeting in private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming in' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is known only to a select inner circle, so hidden from outsiders.

clue.text: Trooper's entrance

definitions.meaning: a trooper (troopship) is a vessel for carrying soldiers; the 's is 'is'
read as en-TRANCE: a rapture or overwhelming delight

explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is not a doorway but the verb pronounced en-TRANCE, rapture; a troopship is one kind of vessel the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a ship carrying troops and an ecstasy of emotion.

clue.text: Overbearing, notorious for holding up work

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: arrant means notorious, utter, as in an arrant knave

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to go is to work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A notoriously domineering boss delaying a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Overbearing people are haughty and presumptuous, a synonym.

clue.text: When the big guns come round, it's to hear virtuosity

indicators.note: come round means turned about, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's big guns
'tis is the poetic contraction of it is
to try a case in court is to hear it

explanation.surface: Skill becomes audible when the artillery arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' is not a sound signal: a judge hears, that is tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is great skill in performance, much as virtuosity is.

clue.text: 'ide in a shady retreat

indicators.note: the apostrophe standing for a dropped h, Cockney style, says to remove H from the word

parts.note: to harbour a fugitive is to hide them

explanation.surface: A Cockney hiding in a shady bower.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ide' mimics Cockney speech, which drops initial H; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a bower of trees or climbing plants giving a cool shaded nook, a synonym.

clue.text: Invent cosmetics

explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means fabricate; as a noun it means face paint.

clue.text: Government grant covering one case

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a patent is a grant from the government of exclusive rights
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: State funding for a single legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal; it is a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's case is a person under treatment, someone being cared for medically.

clue.text: A severe setback, but not a facer

definitions.meaning: a punch landing on the torso, not the face; a facer is a blow to the face

explanation.walkthrough: 'facer' is old slang for both a punch in the face and a sudden setback; the answer is a punch below the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a punch to the trunk, figuratively a serious reverse or disappointment.

clue.text: Steep initially, but approaching the horizontal eventually

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A slope that is steep at the start but flattens out later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like the slope's gradient, but it is the verb to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it in liquid, as one does in a bath.

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: Surprising result found to be transposed

indicators.note: transposed means its two parts swap places

parts.note: to found a company is to set it up

explanation.walkthrough: 'to be transposed' swaps the two halves of SET UP.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is a shock win by the underdog, an unexpected outcome.

clue.text: Roads subject to a change or diversion

indicators.note: a diversion sends things on a changed route, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Roads affected by changes or a traffic diversion.
